q1_issues.issue: "He" has no antecedent, so the witness must be classed person (and stemmed sk_person_1); classing it man reads the referent's kind off grammatical gender, which the instruction set explicitly forbids.
"Gareccio" is the bare, prepositionless direct object of "preached" yet is emitted as a Location on the event, a role the oblique rules license only for a PP that answers where.
Two Location atoms are stacked on one event, whereas the stacked-place rule contains the inner place in the outer one — (LocatedIn gareccio italy) — instead of emitting a second event Location.

The non-restrictive relative ", where he preached" yields no eventuality of its own; it is collapsed into sk_preach_1, so the preaching it predicates of Gareccio is recorded only by accident of the mis-assigned Location.

q2_gaps: Finite locative relative clause ("Gareccio, where he preached"): the instruction set covers reduced/participial relatives and relative clauses in rule premises, but never states how a where-relativizer maps onto the Location role of the relative clause's own event.

A prepositionless place-name object of an otherwise intransitive verb ("preached Gareccio"): the role rules assume either an ordinary participant object decided by the change-of-state test or a PP decided by the question it answers, and cover neither reading of this string.
notes: The spend/exile half is well-formed — Possession for "his exile", Location for "in France", Past on the event, one Name per proper noun. The fronted "in Italy" is a genuine PP and its Location atom is licensed; only the Gareccio atom and the dropped relative are at issue.
